title: Honorarium
text: “What should we do now?”
“Shouldn’t we go help clean up after the waves? We left it all behind yesterday, and I doubt the castle soldiers are going to… clean it up, right?”
“I’m not really sure. But since it’s what Father said, I think it’s a good idea to go check.”
“It’s settled, then. That said, since we don’t plan on returning to the castle town for a while, let’s stop by my dad’s place before we head out. I’d also like to thank him for the weapons.”
“Understood. Then let’s all go together.”
We made our way through the back alleys and stopped by the weapons shop. Father seemed to be just opening the shop door slightly to say hello. We waited for him outside the shop.
“Hey! Isn’t that An-chan! I heard you’ve accomplished quite a lot.”
“Well, yeah. There were a few times I was saved thanks to you, Dad.”
“That makes me happy to hear. What brings you here today?”
“Just dropping by, I guess… Since I did get some financial aid, it might be nice to have you make me a weapon, though.”

“Right now, even if I were to make a new weapon, I don’t have enough materials to begin with—but I think you’d be better off leveling up your party members first. You should be able to manage with your current gear.”
“I guess so. Well… I’ll probably stop by again in a little while, so I’ll count on you then.”
“Sure thing! Hey, An-chan, wait a sec!”
The weapon shop owner stopped my father just as he was about to leave. Hmm? Does he have something else to ask?
“Huh? What’s up?”
“There’s an acquaintance who wants to thank you for your heroic actions yesterday. I’d like you to at least stop by and say hello.”
“Oh, come on… you really don’t need to make a big deal out of it.”
“The folks in Riyute Village think they got off with minimal damage thanks to you, An-chan. They say they can’t do business with a clear conscience unless they thank you.”
“I see… I do tend to hold back a bit when I feel like I owe someone a favor. Alright, I get it… but by that logic, I’d be in your debt up to my ears, Dad.”
“There’s no issue between you and me, An-chan. It’s a business relationship, right? I’m just providing what you asked for.”
“I think you’re selling me good stuff at a fair price, though.”
“I’m satisfied when I do a good job. Don’t be so shy about it.”
“I see… Yeah. Got it.”
It looks like my future Father and my dad are nodding to each other, as if reaffirming their friendship. He really is a generous guy. That’s why it seemed like he even trusted my future Father.
“So, you said you wanted to thank us—which shops are they?”
“Oh, the apothecary and the magic shop. You guys have been there before, right?”

“The apothecary… is that the shop we went to a few times before we started peddling? …And the magic shop is where we got the materials for Sakura-chan’s clothes, right? Let’s go check them out.” We headed straight to the apothecary.
“Um… the old man at the weapons shop told us to come here,”

Father said, addressing the gruff-looking owner of the apothecary. Since they’d only dealt with him a few times before, he seemed a bit hesitant. Still, his expression was gentle—he seemed quite different from his usual self.
“Ah, so you heard about this from the weapons shop? Well, that makes things easy. Some relatives from Riyute Village came by to say you helped them. They asked if you could lend a hand if possible.”
“Ah… I see.”

My father went to speak with him as our representative, and it seems he was given a potion recipe. My father, who’s currently learning to read, said he could make out a little of it. From a quick glance at the recipe book he was given, it was written in considerable detail—covering key ingredients for crafting, mixing ratios depending on the intended use, and the differences between various medicinal herbs.
“I’ll give you the recipes other than the intermediate ones while I’m at it.”
“But—aren’t these… quite expensive, or aren’t they secret recipes or something?”
“They say the village has suffered almost no damage thanks to the Shield Hero and Spear Hero team, don’t they? I’d like to at least do that much.”
“Huh…”
“Besides… it seems you’re making decent sales for something you made by peeking at the recipes, so this is a good opportunity to learn properly, isn’t it?”

My father flinched and recoiled. Ah, so that’s how it was—he’d come here to see which plants were medicinal herbs and, while he was at it, picked up the art of potion-making by watching and imitating. Then, when the weapon shop owner heard that my father was a traveling merchant, he figured out what he was up to—something like that.
“If some amateur tries to make and sell potions without really knowing what they’re doing, it’ll damage our reputation. Learn from this.”
“Y-yes. I’ll do my best to make sure there are no problems.”
“Well, from what I’ve heard, I think you’ll be fine.”

Since I’ll be crafting them using my weaponry skill, problems are highly unlikely. However, it’s true that making them myself can affect the quality—it might be a good way to pass the time during those boring carriage rides. Well, since I’m often leveling up in Siltvelt, I’ll mostly be relying on my skill. My father is quite the perfectionist, so he might use the recipe he received to hone his skills.
“Medicine is bitter, so I hate Kou!”
“Alright, then if I slather this medicine all over myself, Kou won’t come after me anymore.”
“Keel and Kou, don’t do anything weird, okay?”
My father scolds the two of them for sniffing the medicine together. Yuki-chan is sniffing around the area where the herb-infused perfume is displayed, while Sakura-chan looks sleepy.
“It’s such a refined scent, isn’t it?”
“So you sell perfume, too?”
“Just some of it. It’s in the recipe book, so if you’re interested, give it a try.”
“Y-yes. I’ll do my best.”
“Did you stop by the Magic shop?”
“Not yet. I’m thinking of heading over there now.”
“I see. I don’t know what that miser will give you, but be careful.”
“She seemed like a nice old lady, though.”
“That’s his modus operandi. He’s always been that shrewd.”
“Hmm…”
Business is Father’s specialty, you know. He wouldn’t let himself be taken advantage of so easily.

If I recall correctly… I believe that magic shop owner was the one teaching magic to the slaves in the Village of the Future. Well, he’d opened a magic shop even bigger than this one in a town near the village. I remember he had one of my Father’s slaves—whom he’d taken on as an apprentice—working the counter. In that sense, he’s certainly very shrewd.

But is anyone actually losing out on this? Since my Father seemed to have agreed to it, there’s no problem, is there? On the contrary, wasn’t the apothecary the one who was forcibly dragged by the magic shop owner to open a shop on my Father’s estate?

I don’t know the details myself, you know. Filolial-sama and the others loved rumors, so I only heard it from them. Anyway, when I went to the magic shop, the shop owner seemed to be chatting familiarly with my Father.
“Oink!”

I have absolutely no idea what they’re saying. A pig with business acumen is an absolute pain in the neck. You just can’t get through to him. Does he really have business acumen? To me, he just looks like he’s making a racket, oink oink.
“Thank you very much for making Sakura-chan’s clothes. So, what brings you here?”
“Bububu.”
“Ah, magical aptitude?”
“Bububu.”
The magician is looking at Keel.
“Ah, he wants to check Keel-kun’s aptitude.”
“Me? Can I use Magic, too?”
“Oink oink oink.”
Father picked Keel up and made him stare intently at a Crystal Ball, as if the magic shopkeeper were divining his future. After that, Father looked over at me.
“Hey, Motoyasu-kun, do you need to learn Magic?”
“I can already use it.”
After all, I can even use Liberation-class magic—which only Heroes can use. I don’t need to learn it here.
“Huh? You want to see some Magic? Motoyasu, can’t you use any powerful spells that lack potency?”
“Understood. Then I’ll show you one.”
My specializations are fire and healing magic. I can’t use healing magic as specialized as my Father’s, but I can cast high-powered healing spells.
“Liberation Fireheal!”
“Oink!?”
The magic shopkeeper was so startled by the Liberation-class spell I cast that he fell backward.
“A-are you okay!?”
My Father called out to the fallen shopkeeper. The shopkeeper then got back up, shook his head repeatedly, and crossed his arms.
“He said your Magical Power is incredible, Motoyasu-kun. You’re getting praised.”
“Not as much as you, Father.”

Well, when it comes to offensive magic, I’m unbeatable. And this was a healing spell without any enhancements. I still have a long way to go. But if he’s surprised by something this modest, maybe I should show him something more?
“Boo-boo…”
“Boo-boo”
“Right. Since Motoyasu and Elena can already use Magic, there’s no need for them to learn anything new.”
Come to think of it, that Lazy Pig has been tagging along with us for a while now. He’s yawning as if this is a hassle.
“Bub.”
The magic shopkeeper points at Filolial-sama and the others.
“Motoyasu, do we need to teach Sakura-chan and the others magic?”
“Basically, they learn it instinctively, so there’s no need for now.”
Lord Filolial picks up Drifa naturally, too. Apparently, there might be times when we need to teach him depending on the situation, but I haven’t felt any inconvenience so far.
“Bub…”
“Yes. It’s just me and Keel-kun, isn’t it? Is there a problem with that?”
The Magician hands my Father a few books.
“These… aren’t these the ones you asked me to buy last time…?”
“Bubub.”
“Ah, yes. Thank you very much.”

When I asked my Father about it later, he said the Magician gave them to him as a token of gratitude for protecting Riyute Village. Then, finally, the magician gave Father a fragment of some kind of ore. The ore glinted, and Father blinked.
“What was that just now…? I felt something strange…”
“Bub.”
“Ah… so you gave me a fragment of a magic orb as a bonus. You said it would help with learning magic… Thank you for absolutely everything.”
“Bubub!”
The magician, in high spirits, gave Father a few light pats on the back. His demeanor was very gentle.
“W-well, then, we’ll be on our way.”
We left the magician behind. Father placed the book he’d received in the carriage and wiped the sweat from his brow.
“They were all such nice people!”
“Yeah. I’m starting to feel like we’re gradually earning their trust. It feels good to help people in need… but when they’re this kind to us, I start to feel a little guilty.”
“You just have to repay a kindness with a kindness.”
“That’s true. So, let’s go thank the people of Riyute Village, and then we’ll get back to peddling.”
“Yeah! We’ll sell medicine again and help people in need, right?”
Keel smiled and agreed with Father.
“Yeah, that’s how it’ll be. So that everyone can get along like this—just as I told Ren and the people of Siltvelt—let’s do our best to change the country from the inside out!”
We climbed into the wagon where we’d parked it and set off.

Everything is going smoothly. There may be some minor differences here and there, but I’m confident we’re heading in the right direction. Just as Father said, we’ll save as many people as possible before the next wave hits!
Tate and Party’s Good Deeds Points: 15 (5)
